chunks: He is God; there is no god but He. To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him belongs the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.

key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: There is no god but He

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about where all praise and judgement belong?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia tafsir as a bridge between divine attributes and eschatological return, underscores Allah's eternal dominion over both the temporal world (al-ula) and the hereafter (al-akhirah). It reinforces the concept of 'Hakimiyyah' (sovereignty), affirming that all judgment belongs exclusively to God, a theme central to Shia political and theological thought regarding the ultimate authority of the Divine and His Progeny.
